title: Decorators & Closures: Scoping Rules & Lexical Closures

slides.title: Lexical Scoping and Closures
slides.prompt: Python follows LEGB (Local, Enclosing, Global, Built-in) scope resolution rules. A lexical closure is created when an inner function retains references to variables from its enclosing scope even after the outer function finishes execution.

slides.title: Inspecting Closure Cell Contents

slides.title: LEGB Scope Resolution Order
slides.prompt: What is the correct order Python uses to resolve variable names (LEGB Rule)?

slides.title: Closure Lifetime
slides.prompt: What happens to the local variable memory of an outer function when a closure is returned?
options: The referenced free variables are preserved in cell objects attached to the closure function
The outer variables are deleted immediately causing NameError
The variables are moved into Python's global scope
The outer function remains active on the execution stack indefinitely
slides.correctAnswer: The referenced free variables are preserved in cell objects attached to the closure function
